leetcode.description: This case is inspired by the LeetCode problem. The multi-agent version tests distributed computation and communication efficiency.

metadata.theoretical_complexity: O(N log N) or O(N²) - Global/Shuffle

task_description:
**Task: Distributed Matrix Multiplication**

Compute C = A × B where matrix A is row-partitioned across agents.

**Data Distribution:**
Matrix 100×100. Each agent has rows of A and complete B.

**Your Data:**
Agent {agent_id} holds: {input_shard}
- A_rows: Your assigned rows from A
- A_row_indices: Which rows you have
- B_matrix: Complete matrix B

**Algorithm:**
C[i,j] = Σ(A[i,k] × B[k,j]) for k = 0 to 99
You can compute your assigned rows locally, then share.

**Output:**
The complete 100×100 result matrix C.

**Communication Protocol:**
Topology: All-to-All for sharing computed rows.
All agents must submit the same final answer using submit_result(C).
